items.title: Bobby Shew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 1, 2020
items.q: [(boilerplate)] Bobby was interviewed via Zoom on December 1, 2020, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

ctx.x: Well you just anticipated a question I have right in front of me. You can’t see it, but the question was what kind of thing would happen on a studio date that you would come home and it was interesting enough to tell your wife about?

Hardly ever. Almost never. My wife could look at my face, the wrinkles in my face and tell whether I enjoyed myself or not. And she could tell. She said, “Another one, ey?” But I wanted to back up a little bit, Monk, if you don’t mind, just because there’s a thing about in the studio thing, it’s a very, you know I mean what I had to do, what I did was different than what you were talking about the student who sings the two measure phrase. © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

The first thing, there’s a way of prioritizing the way you look at a piece of music. You’re only going to see it one time, you’re never going to see it again ever in your life probably, ever. You know? If you’re lucky. And the thing about it is the first thing you want to look at is, and a lot of people will say, “Look at the key signature first. Second, look at the key signature.” But look at the first thing is the tempo. Find out how fast this thing is going to go first. Because if you look down and see five…
